transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Well, it's good to meet you too. I'm here because... well, I'm having some trouble with eating. What scares me most is that once I start eating, it feels like my hands just keep reaching for more. Even while I’m telling myself, "Tom, stop this right now," I just... I can't seem to stop.
When this happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yes, I do. On those afternoons when I'm alone at the house, I can go through an entire loaf of bread, peanut butter, cookies, whatever leftovers are in the fridge, and a carton of ice cream. It all just happens in one sitting, before I even really look up to see what I've done.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?

Yes, I do. There are times after I eat too much like that where I go to the bathroom and... well, I make myself bring it back up. And I've also taken laxatives, too. I just get so scared that all that food is going to stay in me.
Do the times when you make yourself vomit or take laxatives usually happen after one of those binge-eating episodes?

Yes, they do. It's always after I eat like that. I actually keep a food log, and... well, it shows that for months now, almost every week there's at least one afternoon where I just lose control of my eating. And right after that, I try to fix it by throwing up, or taking laxatives, or just not eating at all for a while. Sometimes I even push myself to do a lot of walking or heavy chores around the house, just trying to make up for it.
